name: Fusion CX Ltd
title: Fusion CX Ltd - 544995 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Fusion CX Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR 5,253 mn, PAT up 31.3% to INR 586 mn, while EBITDA margin fell 110 bps to 18.6% on training costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 5,253 mn (+22.1% YoY, +7.1% QoQ), with 16.8 pp organic and 5.2 pp inorganic (VAP, Australia) contribution. Reported EBITDA was INR 976 mn (+15.2%) at an 18.6% margin, down 110 bps YoY, which management attributes to training costs for two top-five clients ahead of a Q3 ramp-up; management says margin would have been about 20% without it. PAT was INR 586 mn (+31.3%), helped mainly by lower finance cost after the October 2026 listing. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 10,158 mn (+20.4%), with EBITDA of INR 1,927 mn and PAT of INR 1,142 mn.

segments.name: Revenue by geography
segments.commentary: US and Canada 81%, India 9.9%, Europe 4.3%, Australia and others about 4.8% of revenue (as stated on the call).

segments.name: Revenue by delivery model
segments.commentary: Nearshore (Latin America, Eastern Europe, Northern Africa) 39.7%, onshore (US, Canada, Germany) 33.3%, offshore (India, Philippines) about 27%.

segments.name: Core CX verticals
segments.commentary: Telecom and utility 39.2%, BFSI 18.2%, high-tech and travel 16.1%, healthcare 14.5%, others 12% of revenue.

segments.name: AI data infrastructure (Annotera, Roborax)
segments.commentary: About 5% of Q2 revenue, with 18 clients; management targets double-digit share over time. Growing much faster than the core CX business per management; three pilots with top-tier clients in last two months.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue guidance given; management says it aims to maintain and accelerate growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
Q3 FY27 expected to be seasonally stronger than H1, led by healthcare, retail and some telecom, with higher US healthcare enrolment activity and festive promotions.

Margin to recover as training costs roll off: two top-five clients ramp up in Q3, with training billable only after 5-8 weeks of training and production go-live. Management expects EBITDA margin to return to prior levels by end FY27 (some improvement, not a specific number).
Employee cost expected to stay within the current 65%-68% of revenue range, plus or minus 1%.
Australia/NZ expansion (VAP, Philippines delivery) expected to show results in 6-12 months, with possible India delivery added for time-zone fit.
impacx integration over six to eight months; VAP integration over the next few months.
Interim dividend of INR 0.75 per share (75% of face value INR 1) declared on 13 November 2026 for FY26; record date to be announced. First dividend as a listed company.
capex_capacity: Company has about 15,000 people, 42 delivery locations across 14 countries, and serves about 750 customers.
Around 40% of IPO proceeds deployed since listing, mainly debt reduction and the impacx acquisition; balance for platform upgrade, overseas debt repayment, general corporate purpose and acquisitions.
About INR 60 crore raised in the IPO to augment AI data infrastructure investment over two years; about INR 70 crore invested in the Omind AI platform over six years.
AI Data Forge platform for the AI data infrastructure business to be launched within 30 days of the call.

Acquisitions: VAP (Melbourne HQ, delivery from Philippines) completed August 2026; impacx (Western Germany, about EUR 12 mn revenue, about 250 employees, onshore Germany and nearshore Greece) completed about 2-3 days before the call. Both acquired at about 4-4.5x EBITDA.
demand_pricing: Organic growth 16.8% YoY in Q2 and 12.7% in H1; management says these rates are well above the industry average and expects the trend to continue.
Overall growth FY24-FY26 at a CAGR of about 35% including acquisitions.
Top 1 client about 20% of revenue (down from earlier); top 5 at 36.5%, top 10 at 48.9%. Top 5 clients have an average tenure of 13 years, top 10 11.5 years, top 20 10.3 years.
Voice about 70% and non-voice about 30% of Q2 revenue.
Demand for nearshore and onshore contact centres accelerating; strongest traction in the health plan business, with AI data, telecom and BFSI also growing.
Australia targeted at BFSI (mortgage broking, financial planning), plus auto and retail; management cites manpower shortages and better pay there.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand in H2 as training costs for top-client ramp-ups roll off?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Training runs 5-8 weeks including certification and is billed only once clients go into production, so benefits show in Q3 with higher production revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Australia, and is there an opportunity for Indian players?
qa_highlights.answer: Australia and New Zealand face manpower shortages and pay well. The initial focus is BFSI, with auto and retail next; management also plans to add India as a delivery location for time-zone fit, with results expected in 6-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the TCV/ACV and traction in AI data infrastructure?
qa_highlights.answer: No TCV or ACV disclosed. The company has 18 clients in the segment, three top-tier clients in pilots over the last two months, and a pipeline described as very strong without quantification.

qa_highlights.question: What valuation were the acquisitions done at, and is more M&A planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Both FY27 acquisitions were at about 4-4.5x EBITDA. Management says M&A is an ongoing growth lever but gave no specific guidance on further deals.

qa_highlights.question: Why is organic growth lower than the 35% cited, and what is the voice/non-voice and AI mix?
qa_highlights.answer: The 35% is total growth including acquisitions; organic growth was 16.8% in Q2 and 12.7% in H1. Voice is about 70% and AI/DI about 5% of Q2 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth reach about 25% YoY over the next two years, and will margins return to earlier levels by FY27-end?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical growth guidance; management is chasing growth. It expects margins to recover by end FY27 as training costs fall away.

risks_watch: Q2 margin dip from training costs for two top-five clients; Q3 ramp-up must convert into billable production revenue as planned.
Growth is heavily weighted to the US and Canada (81%) and to telecom and utility (39.2%), with top 5 clients at 36.5% of revenue.
AI data infrastructure is about 5% of revenue and needs to scale to the double-digit share management targets; no TCV, ACV or pipeline figures disclosed.
Integration of VAP and impacx, and the earn-out-style consideration tied to impacx performance; watch the Australia and Germany ramp.
Organic growth decelerated from about 35% FY24-26 CAGR (total growth) to 12.7% in H1 FY27; watch whether the organic rate holds.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term growth, AI differentiation and M&A, but cautious on specifics: management declined to give revenue or margin guidance and gave no AI deal values. Tone is notably open on Q3 seasonality and margin recovery timing.
key_quotes: As of now, we are not providing any specific guidance, but as I mentioned in my conclusion, from a go-forward perspective we are chasing growth
Had this expenditure not been incurred, our EBITDA would have been around 20% approx.
Pipeline continues to be very strong.

adds.what: AI Data Forge platform launch for AI data infrastructure business
impacx acquisition (Western Germany, ~EUR 12 mn revenue, ~250 employees, onshore Germany and nearshore Greece)
VAP acquisition (Melbourne HQ, delivery from Philippines)

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management aims to maintain and accelerate growth, with Q3 seasonally stronger and two top-five clients ramping in Q3 and margin recovery by end FY27 (qualitative), backed partly by the VAP and impacx acquisitions, AI Data Forge launch and organic growth of 16.8% in Q2.

oneOffs.what: 5.2 pp of the 22.1% Q2 revenue growth is inorganic (VAP, Australia); organic growth was 16.8%
Training costs for two top-five client ramp-ups depressed Q2 EBITDA margin by about 110 bps YoY (management says ~20% margin without it)

quality.why: Revenue grew 22.1% YoY, of which 16.8 pp was organic and 5.2 pp acquired (VAP, Australia), so the acquisition is roughly a quarter of headline growth; the brief gives no volume figure, and the organic rate slowed to 12.7% in H1, while PAT's +31.3% was helped mainly by lower finance cost after the October 2026 listing, which is not a revenue driver.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell 110 bps YoY to 18.6% on training costs; management says it would have been about 20% without them, and two top-five clients ramp in Q3 with margin expected to return to prior levels by end FY27 (qualitative, no number).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two top-five client ramp-ups in Q3 and acquired capacity from VAP (Aug 2026) and impacx (about 250 employees, about EUR 12 mn revenue) being integrated over 6-8 months, though no new plants or seats are quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic growth was 16.8% in Q2 and 12.7% in H1, management expects the trend to continue, and Q3 is seasonally stronger with healthcare enrolment and festive promotions.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed and no new plant planned; ~INR 60 crore IPO money is earmarked for AI data infrastructure over two years and ~INR 70 crore for the Omind platform over six years, so further capex is plausible but not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue or margin guidance, so there is no baseline to raise; it only said it aims to maintain and accelerate growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 ramp-up must convert into billable production revenue, and training costs for top-five clients drove the Q2 margin dip to 18.6%; any slip in the ramp would push margin recovery out.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI Data Forge platform for the AI data infrastructure business is set to launch within 30 days of the call; the segment is about 5% of Q2 revenue across 18 clients and management targets a double-digit share over time.

rows.label: Australia/NZ expansion (VAP, Philippines delivery)
rows.why: Management expects results in 6-12 months, targeting BFSI, auto and retail where manpower shortages and better pay are cited, with possible India delivery added.

rows.label: AI data infrastructure pilots converting
rows.why: Three pilots with top-tier clients started in the last two months on a base of 5% of Q2 revenue, but no TCV, ACV or pipeline value was disclosed.

rows.label: Interim dividend INR 0.75/share
rows.why: Declared 13 Nov 2026 for FY26 at 75% of face value INR 1, the first dividend as a listed company; record date still to be announced.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term growth, AI differentiation and M&A and open on Q3 seasonality and margin recovery, but declined numeric guidance and AI deal values; analysts pressed on organic growth versus the 35% headline CAGR and on AI mix.
